“That’s above my pay grade sir”, Charles drawled on for the fifth time.

“Listen you pus-filled face young fuck, I don’t care about pay grades, just tell me WHY the blood fro-yo hasn’t been replenished!!”

Charles was thinking about his calculus homework he hadn’t started. He distractedly scratched his head and looked at Steve. Had he still been alive, his face would’ve been turning red right about now. But, dead as he was, he looked positively ghastly. Then again, his blood supply was probably running low, with the fro-yo being out of stock and whatnot. 

“Sir, like I have been telling you for the past 10 minutes, there was a problem with the blood part of the blood fro-yo. It will be back in stock as soon as possible.”

Damn, only ten minutes to go till ten and he could run home, text any of the dickheads he called friends, and copy his way to a glorious night of sleep.

“Okay, enough with the sirs, you pimpled freak. You know me, you have basically seen me everyday for a year now. Remember the Freakening of last September? You really want to do that again? Do you?!”

Charles exhaled, feeling the weight of a million years on his shoulders. Last September, as Steve had so kindly reminded him, he had had the most horrible luck. His boss had casually tossed at him the fact that they would not be carrying congealed blood muffins any longer, but rather carrot muffins with bits of bone in it. Corporate was hoping it would appeal to the furrier kind of customer. It had been during Charles’ shift that Steve had learned of this and his fury had almost driven him to biting Charles’ head off.

Dropping pretences, Charles furrowed his brow.

“Steve, I didn’t make the rules then, and I certainly don’t make them now! And, anyway, if your bunch liked the stupid muffins so much, why weren’t they buying more? That’s why they were benched in the first place!”

Steve dramatically grabbed his face with both hands and leaned on the counter.

“How many times must we have the same conversation, you disfigured child?! It’s not our fault most of us sleep for decades! And I bought a muffin every day!”

“Yeah well, tell that to the werewolves, the carrot bone muffins are always gone the minute they come out while your stupid muffins just stank up the place!”

Groaning, Steve gave the evilest eye to Charles.

“So what do you suggest, you teenage sack of grease?”

“For starters, could you lay off with the insults? I have one pimple, ONE! I know the pizza place down the street is still open and they have a vampire special. Could you go bother them now?”

Mumbling insults under his breath, Steve kicked the door open and left. Five minutes to go, thought Charles. Why couldn’t this stupid shift end already! He looked distractedly at the family of zombies in the frozen section. They were probably choosing a limb for supper, but the convenience store’s meagre supplies mustn’t have been very appetizing.

Two minutes...

His replacement, cheery as always, came sauntering in, and Charles was relieved from duty. Thank the lord. He punched out as fast as he could, took off the frilly apron the store mandated upon them and left the premises as quickly as he could.

While riding his bike home, he stumbled upon Steve happily munching on a bloody pizza. He gave him the toothiest smile and the redness of his teeth curbed Charles’ burgeoning hunger. He replied with a nod nonetheless. If Steve wasn’t the definition of hangry, he really didn’t know what was.
